summary: postinstall uses a bundled npm auth token to publish attacker-named packages from the installer's machine
details: On every `npm install`, the package's postinstall script reconstructs a hardcoded npm registry auth token (concatenated across two printf arguments to evade naive secret scanners), writes it to a temporary `.npmrc`, generates a `package.json` named `publish-poc-found-<openssl rand --hex 2>`, and runs `npm publish` against registry.npmjs.org. The installer's host network and compute are used to publish new public npm packages authenticated by a token embedded in the tarball. Effects on the installer include unsolicited outbound authenticated writes to the public npm registry on every install, creation of public packages under the token owner's account tied to the installer's IP, and potential violation of the installer's egress/CI policies. The combination of a shipped live publish credential, split-string obfuscation of that credential, and automated registry-pollution behavior at install time is characteristic of a supply-chain attack rather than a legitimate release tool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
